correctness.rationale: With the cone blue, the path forcing process is unchanged, and a path-nonforcing set leaves every blue path vertex with at least two white path neighbors. With the cone white, no path-to-path force can occur first, so the first force must target the cone; this happens exactly at a blue endpoint pair or a blue length-three path window. Those triggers then contain a path forcing set. The inspected verifier exhaustively tests every subset for \(2\le m\le17\) and checks both recurrence and coefficient formula; independent brute force reproduced the minimum and minimum-set counts through \(m=7\).

Menon--Singh explicitly cover outerplanar graphs and cones only through coefficient inequalities relevant to the path-extremal conjecture; their cone lemma does not determine the exact center-free trigger set. The binary-word recurrence is therefore additional exact information, not a direct parameter substitution into the checked sources.

value.rationale: Fans are canonical maximal outerplanar graphs and cones over paths, so an exact all-cardinality zero-forcing enumeration is a natural sharpening of the known outerplanar/cone inequalities. The trigger classification is compact, reusable, and yields a nontrivial finite-state recurrence.

final_claim: For the fan \(F_m=K_1\\veeee P_m\), a set containing the cone vertex is zero forcing exactly when its path part is zero forcing in \(P_m\); a center-free set is zero forcing exactly when it contains an endpoint pair or three consecutive path vertices. Hence \(\mathcal Z(F_m;x)=x\mathcal Z(P_m;x)+(1+x)^m-B_m(x)\) with the stated no-\(111\) recurrence and boundary corrections.
limitations: Finite checks are corroborative; the proof is the first-force classification.
